newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WALES MANAGER GOULD CLEARED OF 'RACIST' REMARKS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WALES MANAGER GOULD CLEARED OF 'RACIST' REMARKS.

text.p: The Welsh Football Association (FAW) on Wednesday cleared national team manager Bobby Gould of any impropriety following allegations of racism made by striker Nathan Blake.
Gould's position was thought to be under threat after Blake accused him of making racist comments in training before Wales' World Cup qualifier against Belgium last month.
The manager immediately went on national radio to deny he had been racist but apologised for any "misunderstanding".
Blake's complaint followed a remark by Gould that Blake should wear a black bib in training -- a remark Gould maintains was misconstrued.
A statement from the FAW on Wednesday following a meeting of the eight-man management committee said: "The council has given due consideration to the remarks made by Mr Gould.

"The Council has also taken into consideration a letter from Gordon Taylor, chief executive of the Professional Footballers' Association, expressing his admiration for Mr Gould's expression of apology and his clear explanation of events. The council now considers the matter closed."
Gould took over as manager of the Welsh team at the start of the 1995-96 season. His contract is due to end in December.
FAW president Brian Dear has hinted the contract could be extended through to the European championships in 2000.
